ai.description: *Megophrys himalayana* is a medium-sized frog (40–60 mm) with brown, leaf-mimicking dorsal patterns. It features prominent fleshy "horns" above the eyes and distinct skin folds along the flanks.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys himalayana* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, elongated, horn-like projection on each upper eyelid, which is more prominent than in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Himalayan Horned Frog inhabits moist, broadleaf evergreen forests and temperate woodlands within the Himalayan foothills at elevations ranging from 1,000 to 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Himalayan Horned Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining perfectly camouflaged among leaf litter to ambush passing insects while avoiding detection by predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys himalayana* breeds in streams during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of pigmented eggs attached to the undersides of submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Himalayan Horned Frog occurs in the Eastern Himalayas across Northeast India (Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, West Bengal) at elevations between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Himalayan Horned Frog produces a series of short, metallic "tink" notes with a high pitch, typically heard near small, fast-flowing streams in dense montane forests.
